title: Tommi Pedruzzi’s KDP funnel: content is the front door

# Tommi Pedruzzi’s KDP funnel: content is the front door

A popular publishing thread can look like a book-making recipe. The more useful thing to study is the path around it: public content creates interest, a free training captures intent, and a separate paid offer may monetize the audience. Those are observable mechanics. They do not establish that a particular reader will earn money from publishing.

## What the public trail shows

Tommi Pedruzzi’s X profile describes him as a seven-figure Amazon KDP publisher and links to a free AI-and-eBooks masterclass. His pinned and recent posts use several repeatable formats: a large market claim, a personal earnings claim, a short sequence of steps, and an invitation to request free training. The linked registration page asks for contact details and promotes a scheduled workshop. It also displays student and earnings language alongside a disclaimer that outcomes are not typical or guaranteed.

The claims need to stay in their proper evidence category. The profile and landing page are primary sources for what Tommi says about his business and offer. The public material we inspected did not provide an independently auditable KDP royalty statement, advertising ledger, refund report, or bank settlement that would prove the claimed earnings were net profit. A claim such as “one book earned a large amount” is not a unit-economics model unless period, format, marketplace, royalties, advertising, returns, and operating costs are visible.

The practical pattern is clearer than the financial proof:

1. **Name a specific problem.** The content points people toward a market or reader need rather than asking them to publish any book they happen to like.
2. **Show a sequence.** Posts explain a path from demand research through book creation and launch. A sequence makes the creator’s expertise easier to follow than a string of disconnected tips.
3. **Give a low-friction next step.** The recurring invitation leads to free training. The registration page collects contact information, so the creator has a route to follow up outside the original post.
4. **Connect education to a larger offer.** The free event is a funnel entry point. The exact conversion rate and paid-offer revenue are not public, so the existence of a funnel should not be confused with proven funnel economics.

That is the useful lesson: a content system can sell a method by letting a reader see how the method is organized before asking for a purchase.

## What to measure if we adapt the mechanism

For Anicca, the adapted version should teach a real publishing decision using our own research and examples. A short post can identify one costly mistake; an article can compare the available choices; a free checklist can help a reader act; a paid workbook can provide the complete working sequence. Every step should point to one next action.

Track the stages separately:

| Stage | Evidence to record | What it does not prove |
|---|---|---|
| Post reach | Impressions and watch time from the platform | Interest in buying |
| Profile visit | Platform profile visits | A qualified reader |
| Link visit | Tagged landing-page session | A lead or order |
| Lead | Valid opt-in receipt and source | Attendance or purchase |
| Training | Registration, attendance, and completion | Paid conversion |
| Order | Provider order ID, price, refund state | Net profit until costs settle |
| Contribution | Royalty or collected price minus refunds, fees, ads, and production cost | Repeatability across titles |

Use the same attribution window and source ID across posts, site visits, email signups, and orders. If the free class is the entry point, count registrations and show-ups. If the book itself is the entry point, count product-page sessions and paid orders. Never add likes, followers, and claimed royalties into one “revenue” number.

## A responsible adaptation

We can reproduce the mechanics without reproducing the expression: choose a clearly described reader problem, support demand with current public signals, teach the decision path in our own words, and give each channel one trackable next step. We should not reuse another creator’s thread text, video, visual identity, or earnings claim as our own. If we mention a creator’s result, label it as the creator’s own report and link the original source.

The registration page’s urgency and earnings language may help explain its marketing approach, but it is not evidence that the same language will work for Anicca. A better standard is an accurate offer, a truthful earnings disclaimer, and a useful free resource that qualifies readers rather than promising a payday.

## Sources and evidence limits

- [Tommi Pedruzzi’s public X profile](https://x.com/TommiPedruzzi) — profile statements, public posts, and link to his training.
- [PublishingOS registration page](https://publishingos.io/register-now) — current event funnel, contact capture, and the seller’s own disclaimer.
- [Amazon KDP royalty options](https://kdp.amazon.com/en_US/help/topic/G200644210) — official royalty rules that any earnings example must use.

## Working sheet: trace one content-to-order path

Use one row per post or article. Do not combine posts with different promises or landing pages.

| Field | Entry |
|---|---|
| Source ID and URL | |
| Reader problem | |
| Claim made in the content | |
| Evidence supporting the claim | |
| CTA and destination | |
| Impressions / views | |
| Profile visits | |
| Tagged sessions | |
| Valid opt-ins | |
| Training registrations / attendees | |
| Paid orders / refunds | |
| Collected revenue / fees / ad cost | |
| Follow-up decision | |

### Original article outline

1. State the reader problem in one sentence.
2. Show the decision they need to make.
3. Explain the evidence they can inspect themselves.
4. Give one example with assumptions labeled.
5. Name the risks, costs, and unknowns.
6. Offer a checklist or tool that solves the next step.
7. Link the primary sources and make one relevant CTA.

### Claim register

Before publishing, create one line for every number or earnings statement: exact wording in our draft, source URL, whether it is independently verified or self-reported, time period, unit (gross/net, book/portfolio, revenue/royalty), and the disclosure the reader needs. Remove any number whose source or meaning cannot be stated clearly.

The funnel is doing its job only when provider-backed orders and settled costs can be joined to the content source. A high-reach post with no qualified visits is an attention result. A registration without attendance is a lead result. Neither is a sale.

## Weekly funnel review: find the broken handoff

Calculate each rate from the same source cohort and date window:

- Profile-to-site rate = tagged site sessions / profile visits.
- Opt-in rate = valid opt-ins / tagged site sessions.
- Attendance rate = attendees / registrations.
- Offer conversion = paid orders / attendees.
- Refund rate = refunded orders / paid orders.
- Net contribution = settled revenue − refunds − platform fees − advertising − allocated production cost.

If an event is not exposed by the platform, mark it unavailable. Do not replace missing attendance or order data with engagement. A post can be improved because it attracts the wrong reader, because its CTA is unclear, or because the destination fails to explain the offer. Those are different problems and need separate evidence.

### Original post blueprint

- **Recognition:** describe a precise reader problem in Anicca’s own voice.
- **Useful turn:** teach one decision the reader can make, with a source or example.
- **Next step:** link to the matching article, checklist, or product page.

The pattern is inspired by the path from education to an owned destination, not by any creator’s exact hook, sentence, timing, visual style, or CTA wording. Keep a content ID on the post and carry it through the landing page and order receipt.

Review this table continuously. Increase output only when the next step is working and the cost per settled order is visible. A strong thread is a distribution signal; repeatable, reconciled orders are a business signal.
